subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to design this as a Calder-style hanging mobile, since it's a static model it doesn't need joints. I'll have it hang from a ceiling point with the lowest element resting near the floor at y=0.

For the design, I'm planning black wire arms holding flat colored shapes (red, yellow, blue, black, white discs/leaves) in a recursive balance structure, where each node is a wire down to an arm with two ends that are either shapes or sub-nodes. I'm sketching out a recursive function to build this, defining the arm length, angle, split point, and drop length for each node, and working out how each sub-arm's center offsets below its hanging point.

I'm also figuring out how shapes orient when hanging -- some vertical with their flat plane facing outward, others tilted horizontal like typical Calder discs -- so I can support both orientations in the shape-drawing logic.

For outline shapes, I want a mix of simple geometric forms (circle, ellipse, leaf, triangle-ish) plus an organic "blob" generator using radial noise that stays star-convex so it never self-intersects.

For positioning everything so it sits on the floor correctly, I'm thinking about whether to track the lowest point as I build and shift afterward, or do a dry layout pass first to compute the bounding box, then offset the whole structure so it rests cleanly at the target height.

Now I'm settling on a Calder-style color palette (red, yellow, blue, black, white, with dark wire tones), adding sphere-shaped elements into the mix, and sketching a ceiling hook detail with a small torus ring and rod before working out the branching tree structure hanging below it.

Still defining branch layout...

For the flat disc I'm placing its center slightly below Q with a small wire stub into it, and defining the vertical extent for each shape type (vertical, flat, ball) so I can track the minimum Y across the whole structure. I'm sketching a spec format for blob/ellipse/ball items with scale and seed variation, then planning a walk function that recursively emits geometry while tracking the lowest point for export metadata.
